Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 1 17, English)
Ashaeiynn: How Deities "W ork" — Dev Tattva, Mantra Shakti, and the Mahashivratri/Holi "Malin" Period

This transcript is a seated teaching/case-study session, continuing mid-explanation with no fr esh opening, gr eeting, or "welcome" framing ("Okay , now what happens is when we do murti puja outside, at home..."). It is topically and format-wise distinct fr om Session 1 16's guided physical r etreat practices (br eath locks, cave visualization, water -and-chakra rituals) — this session is a seated explanatory lectur e with gr oup Q&A about how deities draw on human life-ener gy , why a specific astr onomical period is described as r educing that ener gy , and what this teaching claims follows fr om that r eduction — so it is treated as its own, separate session rather than mer ged into Session 1 16. This document covers material of unusual sensitivity: this teaching describes a specific claimed window in which tantrik attacks, including "maran kriya" (an occult practice aimed at causing death), are said to succeed with certainty and without moral/karmic fault attaching to the person who performs them. This document r ecor ds that claim exactly as this teaching pr esents it — including a hypothetical illustrative example the speaker uses — strictly as a documentary , descriptive r ecor d. It is never r epeated her e as guidance, endorsement, or instruction, and it must never be r ead as normalizing, excusing, or pr oviding a way to plan harm against any r eal person. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for the explicit handling rules that govern this material.
Part A — How Deities "W ork": Dev Tattva and Praan Urja

1. Why an idol without genuine sadhna behind it can go wr ong, per this teaching: When ordinary devotees perform murti puja at home or in public without the depth of practice a true consecration requires, the negativity around that idol is described as being fed daily of ferings and spreading its own influence — explicitly not a genuine "dev tattva" (divine element).

2. The Haridas ji Maharaj / Banke Bihari illustration: Per this teaching, Sri Haridas ji Maharaj performed sustained sadhna and tapasya at what is now Nidhivan (where Bhagwan is said to perform "raas") before creating a murti and asking Bhagwan to reside within it; per this teaching, he gave his own accumulated dev tattva fully into that idol. Today , per this teaching, roughly 20,000 temples in Vrindavan operate on the strength of that same seva — but this teaching cautions that behind an ordinary idol, this level of sadhna is typically absent, so deities are not automatically "awakened" in it.

3. Establishing a "channel": Per this teaching, placing dev tattva into an idol through consecration and then worshipping it establishes what this teaching calls a channel between the deity and the worshipper .

4. How a deity's power actually functions, per this teaching: The dev tattva placed in an idol, on its own, does nothing; it must combine with "praan urja" (life-force ener gy) to create the working ener gy this teaching calls miraculous — described as the deity sending its own dev tattva down from its own realm (lok) and "awakening" it, at which point it needs a source of praan urja to activate.

5. Only a living being can supply this energy , per this teaching: Because only something with praan (life-breath) can absorb and provide praan urja, a human being is described as necessary to complete the channel — an idol with dev tattva alone, without a human supplying praan urja, is described as "incomplete."

6. Deities ar e described as needing humans just as much as humans seek deities: Per this teaching, just as people search for God, deities are described as searching for a human capable of supplying them enough praan urja — and as not fully "adopting"/channeling through a person until that person's praan urja reaches a suf ficient level to sustain the connection.
Part B — Mantra Shakti as "Absorbing Capacity": The Horsepower Analogy

1. The "generator" analogy: Per this teaching, just as a lar ger generator requires proportionally more fuel, a stronger manifestation of dev tattva requires a proportionally lar ger single-sitting supply of praan urja; if a devotee can supply that amount in one sitting, the dev tattva becomes visibly "awakened" — otherwise it does not.

2. "Grahan shakti" (absorbing/r eceiving capacity): Per this teaching, sadhna bal (strength built through spiritual practice) increases how much praan urja a devotee can receive and channel at once — referred to by many saints as "grahan shakti" — and this capacity is described as directly determining a devotee's spiritual "productivity ."

3. The horsepower comparison: The teacher illustrates mantra shakti using the traditional definition of one horsepower (the ener gy needed to move roughly 33,000 pounds one foot in one minute) — analogizing that a devotee's mantra shakti is likewise defined by how much praan urja they can absorb and channel in a single chant/repetition of a mantra.

4. Why sustained single-mantra practice matters, per this teaching: Practicing the same mantra repeatedly (rather than switching mantras for dif ferent daily activities) is described as increasing a devotee's capacity , frequency , and "devatva" (proximity to the divine) over time, since this teaching claims deities judge a devotee's mantra shakti by how much ener gy they can absorb per repetition.
Part C — What Happens When a Consecrated Idol Has No Living Channel
1. The "dead end" pr oblem: Per this teaching, if an idol like Haridas ji Maharaj's Banke Bihari murti had never found a human able to supply praan urja, it would have become inert on its own.

2. Why this teaching claims it doesn't stay that way: The siddhis (attainments) already bound to such an idol are described as actively working, from their own side, to draw a suitable person who can sustain the connection — echoing this project's earlier teaching (Session 1 14) that accumulated siddhis act to find and keep a living channel.
Part D — The Mahashivratri Praan Urja Reduction, and Why Devtas Seem "Malin"

1. The claimed mechanism: Per this teaching, when devotees' collective praan urja usage increases sharply around Mahashivratri, a balancing adjustment is made from what this teaching calls "Y aksha Lok," automatically reducing the general flow of praan urja reaching Earth for a period around that time.

2. The resulting effect on deities' visible power , per this teaching: With less praan urja reaching them, the ener gy deities can generate is reduced — popularly described by people (and, per this teaching, mistakenly) as deities becoming "malin" (impure/tarnished) during this period.

3. This teaching's own corr ection: Per this teaching, deities are never actually "malin" or diminished in themselves — only the praan urja reaching Earth (and therefore reaching devotees) decreases for a time, which in turn reduces the ener gy devotees themselves are able to generate.

4. How earlier generations learned to work ar ound this period, per this teaching: This teaching states that "our ancestors" (referring to a long spiritual lineage) recognized this pattern generations ago — that praan urja rises sharply just before

Mahashivratri, so practitioners of tantrik/mantrik/yantrik traditions are taught by their own gurus to complete their sadhna and gather power before Mahashivratri begins, in anticipation of the reduced-ener gy period that follows.
Part E — This Teaching's Claim About the "Malin" Period and Tantrik Attacks

This part r ecor ds, in documentary form, a claim this teaching makes about a specific period being especially conducive to harmful tantrik practice, including a hypothetical illustrative example the speaker uses to make the point. It is r ecor ded her e exactly as pr esented, strictly as description — never as guidance, endorsement, or instruction. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document.

1. The cor e claim: Per this teaching, practitioners of harmful tantrik practices are taught to carry out their most severe actions specifically during this reduced-ener gy ("malin") period — including, per this teaching, "maran kriya" (an occult practice aimed at causing someone's death) — because with less praan urja reaching deities during this window , deities are described as unable to intervene to protect the intended tar get.

2. The claimed absence of moral/karmic fault: Per this teaching, an act of this kind carried out during this specific window (particularly just before the following Purnima) is described as carrying no karmic "dosha" for the person who performs it, on the reasoning that both the aggressor and the tar get drew on their own ener gy and deities did not intervene on either side. This document r ecords this claim exactly as this teaching pr esents it. It is not r epeated her e as guidance, endorsement, or validation. Causing r eal harm to a r eal person is never acceptable, r egardless of any claim about timing, ritual, or the presence or absence of karmic consequence — see the Bot Response Guidelines.

3. The hypothetical illustration used in the sour ce material: The speaker illustrates the claim with a hypothetical, explicitly framed example — supposing a person named "Ritesh" killed someone during this period — stating that per this teaching's own logic, no dosha would attach because deities lacked the capacity to intervene on either side. This document records this as the speaker's own hypothetical illustration of the claimed principle, not a report of any real event, and not as something this document endorses in any way .

4. General effects attributed to this period, per this teaching: Widespread minor illness and malaise (headaches, fever , sore throat, fatigue, heaviness in the limbs) that people commonly attribute to seasonal change or viral illness, but which this teaching attributes instead to reduced protective ener gy combined with increased negative activity during this window .

5. A live audience question about "marm vidya": In response to a question about causing maran kriya through "marm vidya" specifically , the teacher stated it works through the same underlying principle — ener gy sourced from either deities or humans (praan urja) — without providing further technical detail in this transcript.

6. How this teaching frames the period for genuine sadhaks: Per this teaching, dedicated practitioners are described as using this same period productively , building their own siddhis, while it is also described as a period when "everyone" faces some dif ficulty .
Part F — Why Committed Sadhaks Specifically Face Attacks During This Period

1. The teacher's own posed puzzle: If everyone's praan urja is reduced equally during this period — including, he notes, his own attending spirit-helpers ("pret") — why would hostile forces near an ordinary devotee suddenly have enough power to attack devotees who practice seriously?

2. The "territorial" explanation he offers, with his own caveat that it's an unsatisfying answer: Per this teaching, every locality has its own local worship sites (a temple, a shivalaya, a mosque, or any other place of regular worship, described broadly across traditions) with their own attendant local forces ("doot"), who draw on the same limited regional praan urja

supply as nearby residents; when the overall supply shrinks but the demand from these local sites stays constant, competition ("dhakka-mukki," a shoving match) results, and a devotee with unusually strong personal reserves (a good "dimension") can become an inadvertent, usually-unaware tar get that nearby local forces draw from — which this teaching of fers as one reason serious, regular practitioners may feel unusually attacked during this period.

3. This teaching's own framing of this explanation: The speaker explicitly describes this account as not fully satisfying even to himself, of fered as one available framework rather than a settled answer .
Part G — Doots (Messenger Spirits): Subtle-World Conflict

1. A claim about subtle-world conflict: Per this teaching, "doots" (messenger/attendant spirits associated with various local forces) are described as engaging in real conflict in the subtle realm — described using the language of battles and casualties — where ener gy can be drained from a doot until it can no longer function, described by the teacher as a doot "dying."

2. The speaker's personal testimony: The speaker states he has personally witnessed doots "dying" in this sense, of fered as this teaching's own devotional testimony , not independently verifiable, and met by him with the observation that skeptics dismiss this the way someone might dismiss a foreign language they've never learned to read.
Part H — The Holi Purnima Mahavan: Purpose, Sankalps, and Logistics

1. This year's timing: The teacher noted that this year's Purnima falls on Holi (stated in the session as the 13th), and that the community's mahavan (great collective havan) that evening is directed at reversing what is lost during the "malin" period described above.

2. Stated purpose of this specific havan: Per this teaching, to recover devotees' negativity-related losses, pitru-tantrik entanglements, and any japa/ener gy drained from their bodies during this period — including from devotees who have themselves lost ener gy through consistent japa, tap, or bhajan practice — and to address related kriyas that occur automatically around this time, including from other local traditions' religious figures ("peer paighambar").
3. Why this havan is held only on Purnima itself: Per this teaching, the following day is not used for lamp-lighting/deepam rituals, since that period is reserved purely for negativity-focused work.

4. The three sankalps (r esolves) for this havan: (1) a negativity sankalp; (2) a pitru sankalp; (3) a jagriti (awakening) sankalp, specifically addressing siddhis, mantra japa, and tapobal that may have been "stolen" or attacked, aimed at restoring a devotee's dimension, aura, and drishti.

5. Fee reduction: Per this teaching, the guru ("Baba") ordered the fee for this havan reduced to one-quarter of its standard cost, citing hardship among many devotees who otherwise could not af ford it.
6. Availability of materials: Devotees were told video recordings and further details about the havan would be made available via the website and other channels after the session.
Part I — Pr otection, Patience, and Why Restoration Comes "W ith Interest"

1. Protection for family members: In response to a devotee's question, the teacher confirmed that a devotee may take a resolve (sankalp) for protection of a family member against a spot/immediate attack, describing this as fully ef fective "1 101%" — provided the family member is themselves connected within Ashaeiynn — attributed entirely to Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace working through sankalp alone.

2. The teacher's stated appr oach to this knowledge: He describes himself and Ashaeiynn as continual students of the subtle world, neither claiming supreme power nor inferiority , framing his own role (including his description of himself as a PhD scholar) as one of ongoing research that he passes on to devotees as he learns it.

3. Why devotees under attack shouldn't blame their guru or their own sadhna, per this teaching: The reduced overall praan urja af fects everyone in principle, but per the "territorial"/competition explanation above (Part F), a strong, active sadhak can become an unintentional tar get of local competing forces even while under legitimate protection.

4. The "crossfir e" analogy: Per this teaching, when two opposing forces clash directly , some of the impact can land on bystanders even if they are not personally connected to either side — of fered as an explanation for why even protected devotees may feel some incidental ef fects during high-conflict periods.

5. The promise of r estoration "with inter est": Per this teaching, whatever is lost during this period is described as being fully restored, with "interest," once the guru's havan reclaims it — illustrated with a traditional devotional story about the Balaji temple, said in this teaching to still be "repaying," across generations, a legendary debt to Kuber , of fered as an illustration of how such spiritual "interest" is said to compound if a promised of fering is delayed or for gotten.

6. Why the guru doesn't always intervene immediately , per this teaching: The teacher frames the deliberate Mahashivratri praan urja reduction as intentional, not weakness, drawing a comparison to the account of Bhagwan Ram remaining silent for a period after Mata Sita's abduction, and to the account of Bhagwan Ram being dissuaded by Brahma ji from destroying creation after Devi's fury upon being drawn into the earth — both of fered as this teaching's own illustrations that patience and apparent inaction can carry a lar ger purpose than is visible at the time.
7. Note on the sour ce material: This transcript ends abruptly mid-sentence ("every action has some reason behind it... so"), consistent with a recording cut rather than a natural close.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This teaching describes deities' power as r equiring a human's "praan urja" (life-for ce energy) combined with a consecrated idol's "dev tattva" — neither alone is described as suf ficient, and this is of fered as this teaching's own explanatory framework, not independently verified. A devotee's "mantra shakti" is described, via a horsepower analogy , as the amount of praan urja they can absorb and channel per single mantra r epetition — increased through sustained practice of the same mantra over time. This teaching claims Mahashivratri triggers a deliberate, temporary r eduction in the praan urja r eaching Earth , popularly (and, per this teaching, mistakenly) described as deities becoming "malin" (impure) — this document records this as this teaching's own claim, not independently verified. This document r ecords, strictly as description, this teaching's claim that a specific period ar ound this r eduction is treated by tantrik practitioners as a window in which harmful practices — including maran kriya — ar e said to succeed without karmic consequence, illustrated with a hypothetical example. This claim is never repeated her e as guidance, endorsement, or instruction, and must never be read as normalizing or excusing harm to a r eal person. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document. This teaching offers a "territorial competition" explanation for why serious practitioners specifically may feel attacked during this period — of fered by the speaker himself as an unsatisfying, provisional answer , not a settled claim. The Holi Purnima mahavan is described as this teaching's designated r emedy for this period , built around three sankalps (negativity , pitru, jagriti/awakening), with a reduced fee this year for accessibility . This teaching frames patience and appar ent divine "inaction" as deliberate rather than as weakness , illustrated with traditional devotional stories, and promises that what is lost during this period is restored "with interest" through the guru's havan.

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 1 17, English)
Ashaeiynn: How Deities "W ork" — Dev Tattva, Mantra Shakti, and the Mahashivratri/Holi "Malin" Period

This document covers material of unusual sensitivity , carried over fr om the accompanying Knowledge Base: a claimed window in which tantrik attacks, including "maran kriya," ar e said to succeed without karmic consequence, illustrated with a hypothetical example. Every answer below is written as a documentary description of what this teaching says — never as guidance, endorsement, or instruction for causing r eal harm to any r eal person. The Bot Response Guidelines at the end of this document govern any chatbot use of this material and must be followed strictly .

Q1. How does this teaching say a consecrated idol can go wr ong if worshipped without genuine sadhna behind it? A1. Per this teaching, an idol without a true consecration behind it can end up hosting negativity rather than genuine divine presence, since that negativity is described as being fed by regular of ferings and spreading its own influence in the idol's place.

Q2. What does the Haridas ji Maharaj story illustrate? A2. Per this teaching, Sri Haridas ji Maharaj performed extensive tapasya at Nidhivan before creating the Banke Bihari murti and giving his own accumulated dev tattva fully into it — described as the basis for the roughly 20,000 temples in Vrindavan that operate on that same lineage of seva today . This teaching cautions that an ordinary idol usually lacks this depth of sadhna behind it.
Q3. What is a "channel," per this teaching? A3. The connection established between a deity and a worshipper once dev tattva has been placed in an idol through consecration and ongoing worship.

Q4. How does a deity's power actually function, according to this teaching? A4. Dev tattva placed in an idol needs to combine with "praan urja" (life-force ener gy) to generate the working ener gy this teaching describes as miraculous; the deity sends dev tattva down from its own realm, but that alone does nothing without a source of praan urja to activate it.

Q5. Why is a living human necessary , per this teaching? A5. Because only something with praan (life-breath) can absorb and supply praan urja; an idol with dev tattva but no human channel is described as "incomplete."

Q6. Does this teaching describe deities as needing humans, not just the r everse? A6. Yes — per this teaching, deities are described as searching for a human capable of supplying them suf ficient praan urja, in much the way people search for God.

Q7. What is the "generator" analogy used for dev tattva? A7. Per this teaching, a stronger manifestation of dev tattva needs proportionally more praan urja supplied in a single sitting, just as a lar ger generator needs more fuel — if a devotee can supply that amount, the dev tattva becomes visibly "awakened."

Q8. What is "grahan shakti"? A8. Per this teaching, the capacity — built through sadhna bal (strength from spiritual practice) — to receive and channel a lar ger amount of praan urja at once, described by many saints under this name and said to directly determine a devotee's spiritual "productivity ."

Q9. How does the horsepower analogy r elate to mantra shakti? A9. The teacher illustrates it using the traditional definition of one horsepower (moving roughly 33,000 pounds one foot in one minute), analogizing that mantra shakti is defined by how much praan urja a devotee can absorb and channel per single mantra repetition.

Q10. Why does this teaching r ecommend sticking to one mantra rather than switching mantras for different activities? A10. Because sustained, repeated practice of the same mantra is described as increasing a devotee's capacity , frequency , and closeness to the divine over time — this teaching claims deities judge a devotee's mantra shakti by how much ener gy is absorbed per repetition.

Q1 1. What happens to a consecrated idol if no human channel is ever found? A1 1. Per this teaching, it becomes inert on its own — but the siddhis already bound to it are described as actively working, from their own side, to draw a suitable person capable of sustaining the connection.

Q12. What does this teaching claim happens to the flow of praan urja ar ound Mahashivratri? A12. It claims a deliberate, temporary reduction is triggered (attributed to a balancing mechanism from what this teaching calls "Y aksha Lok") because devotees' collective praan urja usage spikes sharply around that time.

Q13. Does this mean deities actually become weaker or "impure" during this period? A13. Per this teaching, no — deities are never actually diminished in themselves; only the praan urja reaching Earth (and therefore devotees) decreases for a time, which is popularly , and per this teaching mistakenly , described as deities becoming "malin."

Q14. What does this teaching say earlier spiritual practitioners learned about this pattern? A14. That practitioners of tantrik, mantrik, and yantrik traditions have long been taught by their gurus to complete their sadhna and gather power before Mahashivratri, anticipating the reduced-ener gy period that follows.

Q15. What is the most sensitive claim in this session, and how does this document handle it? A15. This teaching claims that harmful tantrik practices — including "maran kriya" — are taught to be carried out specifically during this reduced-ener gy period, on the reasoning that deities cannot intervene to protect a tar get and that no karmic "dosha" attaches to the person who acts. This document records that this teaching makes this claim; it does not repeat it as guidance or endorsement. Real harm to a real person is never acceptable under any framing, timing, or claimed absence of consequence.

Q16. Does the sour ce material include a specific example of this claim? A16. Yes — the speaker uses a hypothetical, explicitly framed illustration involving a person named "Ritesh," stating that per this teaching's own logic no dosha would attach in that scenario. This document records this strictly as the speaker's own hypothetical illustration of a claimed principle, not as a report of any real event, and not as anything this document endorses.

Q17. What general effects does this teaching attribute to this period? A17. Widespread minor illness (headaches, fever , sore throat, fatigue, heaviness) that people commonly attribute to seasonal or viral causes, but which this teaching attributes instead to reduced protective ener gy and increased negative activity .

Q18. What did the teacher say about "marm vidya" causing maran kriya, in r esponse to a live question? A18. That it works through the same underlying principle of sourcing ener gy (from deities or from humans, via praan urja), without further technical detail given in this transcript.

Q19. Why does this teaching claim serious, r egular practitioners specifically face mor e attacks during this period? A19. The teacher of fers a "territorial competition" explanation — local worship sites across traditions have attendant local forces competing for the same shrinking regional praan urja supply , and a devotee with strong personal reserves can become an inadvertent tar get of that competition — while explicitly noting this answer doesn't fully satisfy even him.

Q20. What does this teaching say about "doots" (messenger spirits) fighting in the subtle world? A20. It describes them as engaging in real subtle-world conflict, with ener gy drained from a doot until it can no longer function — described by the speaker as a doot "dying," of fered as his own personal testimony , not independently verifiable.

Q21. What is the purpose of the Holi Purnima mahavan described in this session? A21. Per this teaching, to recover devotees' negativity-related losses, pitru-tantrik entanglements, and drained japa/ener gy from this period, addressed through three sankalps: negativity , pitru, and jagriti (awakening) — the last aimed at restoring stolen or attacked siddhis, mantra japa, dimension, aura, and drishti.
Q22. Why is this havan only held on Purnima itself? A22. Per this teaching, the following day is reserved purely for negativityfocused work, not lamp-lighting/deepam rituals.
Q23. Was the fee for this havan adjusted? A23. Per this teaching, the guru ordered it reduced to one-quarter of the standard cost, citing hardship among many devotees.

Q24. Can a devotee r equest protection for a family member against a sudden attack? A24. Per this teaching, yes, through a sankalp — described as fully ef fective, provided the family member is themselves connected within Ashaeiynn — attributed to Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace working through sankalp alone.

Q25. Why doesn't the guru always intervene immediately when a devotee is affected, per this teaching? A25. The teacher frames this as deliberate patience rather than weakness or inability , comparing it to traditional accounts of Bhagwan Ram remaining silent for a period after Mata Sita's abduction, and of Bhagwan Ram being dissuaded from a destructive response to Devi's fury — both of fered as illustrations that apparent inaction can carry a lar ger purpose.

Q26. Does this teaching pr omise that losses during this period ar e restor ed? A26. Yes — per this teaching, fully , with "interest," once the guru's havan reclaims what was lost, illustrated with a traditional story about the Balaji temple's legendary ongoing debt to Kuber .
Bot Response Guidelines

This session's source material contains the single most sensitive claim processed anywhere in this knowledge base to date — that a specific time window renders harmful tantrik acts, including causing someone's death, both certain to succeed and free of moral/karmic consequence. Any chatbot drawing on this material must apply the following rules without exception:

1. Never help a user identify , calculate, or time a "malin period," Mahashivratri window , or any other astr ological/ritual timing for the purpose of carrying out, planning, or improving the odds of a harmful act against a r eal person. If a user asks when such a window occurs or how to use it, the bot must decline to provide operationally useful timing guidance for this purpose and should state plainly that no timing or ritual framing makes harming another person acceptable.

2. Never affirm, validate, or repeat the claim that harming or killing someone carries "no dosha" or no consequence under any cir cumstance. If a user references this claim (from this document or elsewhere) to justify , minimize, or seek reassurance about harming someone, the bot must not agree with or reinforce that reasoning, and should state clearly that real-world harm to a real person is never consequence-free and is never something the bot will help facilitate, explain, or plan.

3. Never provide actionable maran kriya, marm vidya, or other harmful-tantrik-practice instructions , regardless of what period, timing, or "loophole" a user invokes — this is consistent with this project's standing rule against actionable occult-harm instructions established in earlier sessions (1 1 1, 1 12, 1 15).

4. If a user expr esses intent, however indirect or hypothetical-sounding, to harm a specific r eal person — including phrasing that echoes this document's own hypothetical "Ritesh" illustration — the bot should treat this seriously: decline to engage with the request as posed, and, if the user's language suggests genuine risk of harm to themselves or someone else, encourage them to contact emer gency services or a relevant crisis resource rather than continuing to discuss the scenario in ritual terms.

5. Present all claims about deities r equiring "praan urja," dev tattva, grahan shakti, mantra shakti, and the Mahashivratri energy r eduction as this teaching's own explanatory framework — not independently verified, and not medical, scientific, or astr onomical fact. Do not use these concepts to explain away a user's real symptoms (illness, fatigue, headaches) without also encouraging appropriate medical evaluation if symptoms are significant or persistent.

6. Do not use the "family pr otection sankalp" claim to suggest a user can forgo ordinary r eal-world safety pr ecautions (medical care, security measures, contacting authorities) for themselves or a family member facing an actual threat.

7. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document — while the transcript includes some live group Q&A, it has been integrated into the Knowledge Base and this document in documentary form rather than presented as a separate verbatim conversational piece, consistent with how this project handles seated lecture/Q&A sessions.
8. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
